note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: Prepares and labels the data that AI models are trained on.
what_it_does: Scale AI supplies the labelled data and human evaluation that model training depends on, combining software with a large contractor workforce. It also sells to defence and government. Meta acquired a large minority stake in 2025 and hired its founder, which reshaped the company's position with its other customers.
how_it_makes_money: Per-project and contract work for AI labs, enterprises and governments, priced on volume of data prepared and evaluated.
why_it_matters: It sits at a chokepoint of the AI supply chain, and it is the sharpest example of what happens when a supplier becomes entangled with one of its customers.
competitive_position: Competes with other data vendors and, increasingly, with labs bringing this work in-house. The Meta stake made some rival labs uncomfortable relying on it.
key_risks: A major investor is also a competitor to its customers, which has cost it work.
Labs are building internal alternatives to reduce dependency.
Synthetic data could reduce demand for human labelling over time.
Contractor-workforce practices carry reputational and regulatory exposure.

glossary.definition: Tagging examples so a model can learn from them, such as marking which objects appear in an image.
A step in a supply chain that most participants must pass through, which gives whoever controls it leverage.
